Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The Zimbabwe players are making their way out in the middle. Vikramjit Singh and Max O'Dowd, the two openers for Netherlands are already out there. Richard Ngarava to start proceedins with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Zimbabwe have posted a respectable total here and keeping in mind that they bowled out Netherlands for 191 in the warm-up game, they will confident of defending this with the momentum and the crowd also behind them. Netherlands know that they could have been chasing a lot lesser, but now will have to bat their skins out to take a lead in the series. It will be a really exciting chase to watch and join us in a bit to see how it unfolds.

Netherlands will feel like they let this slip away from them as they were in pole position when they reduced the hosts to 98-7. The duo of Fred Klaassen and Paul van Meekeren used the conditions really well and extracted some extra bounce which really troubled the hosts as they could not handle it. However, Scott Edwards missed a trick in the middle overs bowling too much spin and allowed the hosts to get back in the game and post a really good total which wasn't at all looking likely after the first 20 overs. This shows that they still have a lot to learn and not give the opposition any opening when they are on top, As experineced teams will always punish whenever they get the opportunity. Fred Klaassen was the pick of the bowlers with three wickets while Paul van Meekeren picked up a couple of scalps. Brandon Glover, Vikramjit Singh and Shariz Ahmad all chipped in with one each.

Zimbabwe showed immense fight and character with the blade. They were pushed on the back foot right from the start as their top-order were already back in the hut inside the first Powerplay. They were reduced to 70-5 and then 98-7 and were starring down the barrel. However, two heroes, Wellington Masakadza and Clive Madande stepped up for them and slowly and steadily repaired their innings and built a great partnership for the eighth wicket. They looked unfazed by the Netherlands attack and added a crucial 70 runs together before a lapse of concentration ran Masakadza out. That did not effect Madande as he got good support from Richard Ngarava who played a few lusty blows and both of them built another fifty-run partnership. In the end, Clive Madande finished with a well made 74 and Zimbabwe managed to get close to 250.

An excellent recovery from Zimbabwe! They needed someone to step up, and Clive Madande did exactly that and how. He notched up his maiden-ODI half century and helped his side comeback from a precarious situation. Netherlands will be disappointed, and now has huge task on their hands to get the win.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Finally Netherlands bowl Zimbabwe out. This is short and on middle, Clive Madande leans back and looks to pull but this hits high on his bat and balloons behind the wicket. Scott Edwards takes a good catch diving in front to dismiss him. Zimbabwe finishes 249/10.
Commentary.Howout: c Scott Edwards b Fred Klaassen

Short of a length and on off, Wesley Madhevere guides it through point for one.
Overpitched and on off, Wesley Madhevere drills it towards mid off.
Pitched up, on middle, Sikandar Raza knocks it in front of mid on for a quick single.
Slight Halt! Wesley Madhevere has been hit on his waist while trying to pull one and is receiving some treatment. We are ready to continue.
Short and around leg, Wesley Madhevere goes for the pull, but gets hurried and misses as the ball defelcts off his waist towards the square leg region. A leg bye is taken.
Back of a length and on off, Wesley Madhevere keeps it to the off side.
FOUR! Up and over! This is back of a length and outside off, Wesley Madhevere frees his arms and cuts it over point for a boundary.
Full and on middle, Wesley Madhevere nudges it through square leg for one.

FOUR! SMASHED! Fred Klaassen lands this short and on middle, this time it sits up nicely, Wesley Madhevere gets into postion quickly and hammers it of the middle of the bat towards the deep mid-wicket fence for a boundary. That went like a bullet to the fence.
Fuller again and around leg, Sikandar Raza misses his flick as the ball goes off his pads towads square leg. A leg bye is taken.
Goes a bit fuller and on middle, Sikandar Raza defends it to the leg side.
Back of a length and on off, extra bounce again, Sikandar Raza somehow manages to keep it out.

DROPPED! Wesley Madhevere gets a life there! This is full and outside off, Wesley Madhevere reaches for it and slices it uppishly towards backward point where the fielder is a bit late to react and the ball burst through his hands. A single is taken.
Back of a length and around off, Sikandar Raza punches it towards cover-point.
Full and on middle, Sikandar Raza knocks it down the pitch.
This is on a good length and on middle, Sikandar Raza blocks it out.
Sikandar Raza walks out next.

OUT! TAKEN! The extra bounce has done the trick again for Netherlands. They are right on top here. Paul van Meekeren bangs this onto the pitch around off, rises up viciously, Innocent Kaia tries to keep it out, but gets surprised and is in an awakward position as the extra bounce takes the outside edge and goes towards second slip where Colin Ackermann leaps up and grabs it. Zimbabwe three down and in a spot of bother now.
Commentary.Howout: c Colin Ackermann b Paul van Meekeren

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on off, Innocent Kaia steers it towards backward point.
FOUR! Good shot! Paul van Meekeren lands this short and on middle, Innocent Kaia gets on top of the bounce and swivels and pulls it towards the deep mid-wicket fence for a boundary.
Short and on middle, Innocent Kaia pulls it towards deep square leg for a single.
Back of a length and on off, Innocent Kaia punches it towards mid off.
Fred Klaassen serves this full again, on leg, shaping in, Innocent Kaia misses his flick and gets hit on the pads. There is a stiffled appeal for LBW, but turned down.
Pitched up, on off, Innocent Kaia pushes it towards mid off.
Full again and on middle, Innocent Kaia blocks it down the pitch.
Full and on middle, Innocent Kaia works it towards short mid-wicket.

An appeal for caught behind, and the Netherlands players think they have got their man, but the the finger stays down. Paul van Meekeren lands this short again and on middle, Wesley Madhevere tries to lift his bat to leave it, but the ball hits his elbow and goes behind where Scott Edwards pouches it safely. They think that that the sound is from the bat, but in the end Wesley Madhevere is safe.
Another bouncer, on middle, slower too, Wesley Madhevere goes through his pull shot early this time, and missse again.
Paul van Meekeren bangs in a bouncer, on off, Wesley Madhevere goes for the pull shot, but fails to connect. The umpire signals a wide for height.
Back of a length and on off, Wesley Madhevere knocks it towards short covers.
FOUR! Lovely shot! Paul van Meekeren bowls a bit fuller and outside off, Wesley Madhevere accepts the width and opens the face of his bat to cream it through backward point for a boundary.
On a length and on middle, Wesley Madhevere blocks it out.
Paul van Meekeren strays away from his line, and serves this full and down the leg side, Wesley Madhevere misses his flick. Wided.
This is on a hard length and on off, Wesley Madhevere leaves it alone as Scott Edwards takes it near his chest.
On a length and on off, Wesley Madhevere guides it through backward point for a run.

Extra bounce again! This back of a length and on middle and leg, rises after hitting the deck, Wesley Madhevere gets surprsied as he tries to keep it down, but the ball loops up off the bat and falls on the pitch.
Fuller in length and around off, Wesley Madhevere leaves it alone.
Overpitched and on middle, Innocent Kaia flicks it through square leg for one.
Fred Klaassen bangs in a bouncer, on middle, Innocent Kaia goes for the pull, but gets hurried and gloves it down onto the pitch.
Fullish and on middle, shaping in, Innocent Kaia works it towards mid-wicket.
Wesley Madhevere walks out next.

OUT! TAKEN! Paul van Meekeren strikes now! A huge wicket for Netherlands, and Gary Ballance stands there in disbelief. Paul van Meekeren bangs this onto the pitch and around off, Gary Ballance moves across a bit to push it away, but gets hurried due to the extra bounce and the loops up off the top edge towards backward point where Shariz Ahmad runs to his right to take a dolly. Zimbabwe two down now!
Commentary.Howout: c Shariz Ahmad b Paul van Meekeren

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nice shot! Paul van Meekeren bowls this a bit too full and around off, Gary Ballance shows the full face of the bat to drive it sweetly through covers for a boundary.
Back of a length and on middle, Gary Ballance tucks it towards short mid-wicket.
This is pitched up, on off, Gary Ballance drills it towards mid off.
Paul van Meekeren bangs in a sharp bouncer, on middle and leg, Gary Ballance ducks underneath it.
Full and on off, Innocent Kaia drives it wide of mid off for a single.
Touch fuller and outside off, shaping away, Gary Ballance leaves it alone. End of a successful over for Netherlands.
Fred Klaassen continues to bowl on a good length, on off, Gary Ballance knocks it in front of point.
Length again and on off, Gary Ballance keeps it out to the off side.
On a length and on off, Gary Ballance steers it towards point.
Gary Ballance walks out at no.3.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Fred Klaassen draws first blood! A beauty of a delivery to get rid of Ervine. This is on a hard length and pitches on the off stump line, nips away sharply with some extra bounce, Craig Ervine looks to block it out, but the movement away and the bounce takes the outside edge and Scott Edwards behind the stumps takes a sharp catch to his left. Zimbabwe lose their first wicket.
Commentary.Howout: c Scott Edwards b Fred Klaassen

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Craig Ervine gets off the mark in style! Fred Klaassen serves this full and just outside of, Craig Ervine stays there and drives it firmly through extra covers for a boundary.
Touch fuller and on the sixth stump line, Innocent Kaia decides not to play at it again.
On a length and around off, shaping further away, Innocent Kaia leaves it alone.
Overpitched and on off, Innocent Kaia knocks it to the left of the bowler.
Goes a bit fuller and on off, Innocent Kaia pushes it towards point.
This is on a hard length and on around off, swinging away, Innocent Kaia lifts his bat and lets it go to the keeper.
Paul van Meekeren begins with a short delivery, on middle, Innocent Kaia pulls it wide of deep square leg for a couple of runs.
Paul van Meekeren will bowl from the other end.
This is on a good length and on middle, Craig Ervine keeps it out to the leg side.
Short again and outside off again, Craig Ervine offers no shot at it.
Short of a length and outside off, shaping away, Craig Ervine leaves it alone.
Fuller one and on middle, Innocent Kaia nudges it through square leg for a single.
Back of a length and around off, Innocent Kaia punches it towards covers where the fielder dives over it and lets it through. Two runs taken!

FOUR LEG BYES! Zimbabwe are underway with extras! Fred Klaassen starts with a full delivery, but down the leg side, Craig Ervine tries to tickle it away, but misses as the ball goes off his pads towards the fine leg fence for a boundary. Not the start that Fred Klaassen was looking for.

Done with the pre-match formalities! So the players are out in the middle and the players of Zimbabwe follow the Black Lives Matter movement by going down on one knee. Innocent Kaia will be on strike along with Craig Ervine on the other end for Zimbabwe. Fred Klaassen will open the bowling for Netherlands.

We are moments away from the start of the game, but first the players of both teams line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Netherlands' first followed by the national anthem of Zimbabwe.

Craig Ervine, the captain of Zimbabwe says that it looks a good wicket and will mostly be the same for both teams. Adds that it is crucial to get through the first 8 overs and then capitalise on it. Tells that it is nice to have a lot of cricket being played which is good for the players to gain experience.

Scott Edwards, the skipper of Netherlands says they will bowl first as the pitch might well remain similar throughout the day. He adds the team has had a month's preparation and is looking forward to this series. He closes by saying that they will be looking to chase whatever is posted in front of them and the wins they have against Zimbabwe means nothing as that was in totally different conditions in the past.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Innocent Kaia, Craig Ervine (C), Wesley Madhevere, Gary Ballance, Sikandar Raza, Ryan Burl, Wellington Masakadza, Clive Madande (WK), Brad Evans, Richard Ngarava, Blessing Muzarabani.

Netherlands (Playing XI) - Vikramjit Singh, Max O'Dowd, Tom Cooper, Musa Ahmad, Colin Ackermann, Scott Edwards (C)&(WK), Teja Nidamanuru, Shariz Ahmad, Paul van Meekeren, Fred Klaassen, Brandon Glover.
TOSS - Netherlands have won the toss and they have elected to BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Darlington Matambanadzo is pitchside. He says that the sun is shining and outfield is fast. Adds that wicket looks really nice and there is a nice balance of moisture. Reckons it will be good for batting, but says that chasing could turn out be a better option as the seamers might get some help up-front.

Netherlands, on the other hand do not have a good record in this format and they will hope to change that. The batting line-up has been inconsistent, and the bowling attack lacks teeth which is a major problem for the team. They take on a stronger side, and Scott Edwards would like his players to play positively in this game. Let's see who comes out on top. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

Craig Ervine will look for a determined effort from his players and take an early lead in the series. They know the conditions and have a strong batting line-up. Craig Ervine would want the senior players to lead from the front and guide the side to a win. The addition of Sikandar Raza also gives them a massive boost.

Hello and a warm welcome folks! We are here for the first ODI of this three-match series between Zimbabwe and Netherlands which will be played at the Harare Sports Club. Zimbabwe drew their last ODI series against Ireland at home. Netherlands is returning to this format after nine months and has been winless since 2021. This a good opportunity for both teams to test their squads in this format with the World Cup not that far away.
